title: Picture Equations
big_idea: A shape is a hidden number, and the same shape is always the same number
child_idea: In a picture equation each shape is a number. The same shape is always the same number. We find the number, then check it in every line.

moe.strand: Addition and Subtraction; Multiplication and Division (reasoning about equality)
topics: A number sentence with a missing number and "=" as the same amount on both sides (Primary 1, Addition and Subtraction, p. 31)
Multiplication within 40 (Primary 1, Multiplication and Division, p. 31)
A symbol that stands for an unknown number, and taking one line from another (letters for unknowns are Primary 6, p. 43)
moe.note: Strand label for the tutor only. BEYOND PRIMARY 1 ON PURPOSE. One line with one hidden number (like 4 + box = 10) is Primary 1 work and fills Start here. Using the same shape in two lines, taking one line away from another, checking an answer in every line and a times line are not taught at school at this age (letters for unknowns are Primary 6, p. 43): this lesson uses drawn shapes and boxes only, never letters, always with counters or cups to hold the numbers. Think harder (two shapes, two lines) and Go further (three shapes, a times line, a sum and a product) go past the school Primary 1 syllabus. Owner decision, 22 Oct 2026: strong content with scaffolding, said plainly to families. Say this on the parent page and in the opening of the guide; do not describe the lesson as MOE-aligned or syllabus-aligned. Reading order for a times line: heart × circle is heart groups of circle; either order is accepted. Contest tag (tutor only): symbol equations and substitution; taking one line from another.

contest_moves: a symbol stands for one number in every line
take one line from another to find a shape
check the answer in every line
a sum and a product together
objectives: Say that a shape in a picture equation is a hidden number, and that the same shape is the same number in every line.
Find one hidden number in a line such as circle + square = 10 when the square is known, and in a line such as heart + heart = 14.
Check an answer by putting the number back into the line.
Think harder: use two lines about the same shapes (take one line from the other) and check the answer in both lines.
Go further: a times line, three shapes at once, and a sum and a product together.

remember: A box in a number sentence hides a number: 6 + box = 10 (Term 1, taught again with a ten-frame)
The same number twice: box + box = 12 (taught again with two equal plates)
4 groups of 5 as 4 × 5 (Term 2 Lesson 5, taught again with a picture)
joining_cold.assumes: Only counting to 20 and adding small numbers. Nothing from an earlier lesson is needed: the warm-up shows the ten-frame, two equal plates and four bags with a picture, and the × sign is said again as groups of. The word shape stands for a number is taught in Explore.
joining_cold.note: Fairly safe to miss, with one exception: the Term 2 Lesson 10 check has one picture-equation question (a heart + heart total and a friend's number to check). A child who misses this lesson watches the recording and does workbook pages 1 and 2 before the check. A child who joins here without Term 2 Lessons 5 and 6 can follow, because the warm-up shows groups of and the times sign again, and the times lines are in Think harder and Go further only.

child: The printed workbook with the ten-frames and counters kit page (page 6): a grown-up cuts out the 20 counters beforehand
About 30 small things of one kind (counters, buttons, dry beans or pasta) in case more counters are needed
4 small pieces of paper (shape cards): a grown-up draws a circle, a square, a triangle and a heart, one on each piece (the star in some questions needs no card)
A pencil, a rubber and spare paper
tutor: A set of paper shape cards (a circle, a square, a triangle and a heart), a cup and some counters to show on camera if you wish
kit_pages: Ten-frames and counters (page 6): 20 counters to cut out, 10 red and 10 yellow, and four ten-frames to lay counters on
materials.notes: No ruler is needed. Nothing needs to be bought: everything can be found at home. No matches, toothpicks or anything sharp. Small things never go near the mouth or ears; keep them away from younger brothers and sisters. Cups stay on the table.

timing.notes: Opening is 2 minutes (the routine and rules were taught earlier in the term; give the recording, muting and camera notice). Explore has 12 minutes: a shape and a pile of counters, the same shape twice, then two lines about the same shapes. The mini-lesson has 12 because it states the three rules, finds a shape, takes one line from another, checks in both lines and shows one times line. The workbook has 30 minutes because Start here takes a middle child about 18 minutes: pages 3 to 5 are for home for most children. The last 5 minutes are the standing buffer; the optional Go further slide is used only if the lesson is on time.
skip_order: Start with: cut the times line slide (s-m4) in the Mini-lesson to one question
Then: shorten Explore round 3 to the circle only
Then: take the extra minutes from the flex time

sneak_peek.q1: A cup hides some counters. The cup and 4 loose counters make 9 counters in all. How many counters are in the cup?
sneak_peek.q2: Each shape is a number. The star + the star = 14. The heart + the star = 10. Find the number for the heart. Write it.
sneak_peek.a2: 3. The two stars make 14, so one star is 7. The heart and 7 make 10, so the heart is 3.

opening.say: If you are watching the recording: hello! Get a pencil, paper, your workbook, shape cards, counters and two cups. Pause or rewind any time.
opening.action: Gather your workbook, shape cards, counters, two cups, pencil and paper. Press play when ready.

remember.say: Recording: join in! Say your answers out loud before I say them. Pause if you need longer.
remember.action: Play along. Say each answer out loud before the video does.

sneak.say: Recording: pause now and try both puzzles on your paper. Guessing is fine. Press play for the next part.
sneak.action: Pause. Try both puzzles on your own paper. A guess is fine.

explore.say: Recording: pause now. Use counters and your shape cards to find each hidden number. Press play when you have tried.
explore.action: Pause. Put counters on the shape cards to find each hidden number, then check it.

mini.say: Recording: keep watching and copy the examples. Rewind if you miss a step.
mini.action: Watch and copy the examples. Rewind any step you missed.

break.say: Recording: stand up and join in! Count to 20, clap on 5, 10, 15 and 20, and whisper the rest.
break.action: Stand up. Clap on 5, 10, 15 and 20 and whisper the numbers in between.

work.say: Recording: pause now and do workbook page 1. When you finish a page, press play to check it.
work.action: Pause. Do page 1, then play to check. Then page 2. Then choose a page to try.

talk.say: Recording: pause. Tell a grown-up if Aisha is right, and test it with counters.
talk.action: Pause. Explain your answer to someone at home, and test it with counters.

exit.say: Recording: pause and do the exit ticket on your own. Then press play to check it.
exit.action: Pause. Do the exit ticket alone, then play to check it.

look.say: Recording: pause and fill in your look-back box. You can pass.
look.action: Pause. Fill in the look-back box, or pass.

flex.say: Recording: well done for finishing! Show a grown-up one thing you found out.
flex.action: Show a grown-up your workbook and tell them one thing you found out.

slides.title: Picture Equations

blocks.head: TODAY WE WILL
items: Find the number a shape is hiding.

slides.note: Lesson 9 of Term 2, 90 minutes. Objective: find a hidden number behind a shape in a picture equation, know that the same shape is always the same number, check the answer in every line, and take one line away from another. Plain statement for families: one line with a hidden number is Primary 1 work, but using the same shape in two lines, taking one line from another and a times line go past the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. Shapes and boxes only, never letters. Time plan: opening 0 to 2, warm-up 2 to 8, sneak-peek 8 to 12, explore 12 to 24, mini-lesson 24 to 36, brain break 36 to 40, workbook 40 to 70, talk 70 to 76, exit ticket 76 to 82, look-back 82 to 85, flex time and goodbye 85 to 90 (the buffer: do not start anything new). Think harder, Go further and the Investigation are for every child to choose. Say the recording notice in one line: you and the screen only; a child may keep the camera off.
slides.subtitle: A shape hides a number

mascot.say: Hi, I'm Mi. Let's notice, test and explain why!

slides.title: Warm-up: a box hides a number

blocks.text: Touch the counters. Say the number in the box.

slides.note: Six counters sit in a ten-frame that holds ten. The box hides how many more fill it. Ask: how many more fill the frame (4); the box in the second line (5); the box in the third line (4). Children answer aloud or with fingers. No writing, no marks. A child who is unsure touches each counter, counts the empty places (children may lay counters on a ten-frame of the kit page), or holds up fingers for the first number and counts on.

mascot.say: A box can hide a number!

slides.title: The same number twice

blocks.text: Two plates with the same number of counters.

slides.note: Two plates with the same number of counters. Twelve counters in all. Ask: what is 5 + 5 (10); box + box = 8, the same number twice (4); 7 + 7 (14). Children answer aloud. A child who is unsure deals counters one at a time onto two plates, or uses fingers on two hands. The same number twice is a double: it comes back with the hearts in Explore.

slides.title: 4 groups of 5

blocks.text: 4 × 5 means 4 groups of 5.

slides.note: Four bags with five counters in each bag. We add one bag at a time: 5, 10, 15, 20. Ask: how many counters in 4 bags of 5 (20); 3 groups of 4 (12); 2 groups of 10 (20). This is Term 2 Lesson 5 taught again: the × sign says groups of. A child who is unsure counts the counters one bag at a time, saying the total each time.

slides.title: Sneak-peek puzzles

blocks.text: Ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start. Nobody is marked.

cols.head: PUZZLE 1: anyone can try
items: A cup hides some counters.
The cup and 4 loose counters make 9 in all.
How many counters are in the cup?

cols.head: PUZZLE 2: think
items: Each shape is a number.
How many is the heart?

slides.note: Puzzle 1 (a cup and 4 counters make 9; the cup holds 5) is an access question: any child can count out 9 and take 4 away. Puzzle 2 is a thinking question on the lesson idea: two stars make 14, so a star is 7, and the heart and a star make 10, so the heart is 3. Say: two sneak-peek puzzles, ideas we have not learnt yet; a guess is a great start and I do not know is welcome; nobody is marked. Children write on their own paper. Nobody holds paper to the camera. There is no private chat. Answers: 5; 3. Do not reveal puzzle 2 until Talk time. Do not write scores or keep a list.

slides.title: Explore: a shape and a pile

items: Count out 10 counters.
Put 4 on the square card.
The rest go on the circle card. How many?

slides.note: Round 1, about 5 minutes. Children use their shape cards (small papers with a circle, a square, a triangle and a heart drawn on them) and counters (the kit page counters or small things). The picture says circle + square = 10, and the square is 4. They count out 10 counters, put 4 on the square card and the rest on the circle card, then count the circle card (6). Say: the circle is 6. Write circle = 6 on the screen, then check: 6 + 4 = 10. If a family has no cut-out cards, a cup or a piece of paper with the shape drawn on it works. Answer: 6. Do not name a child with a wrong answer.

slides.title: The same shape twice

items: Count out 12 counters.
Share them onto 2 heart cards, one at a time.
The piles must match. How many on one heart?

slides.note: Round 2, about 5 minutes. Heart + heart = 12. Both hearts are the same number, so the piles must match. Children deal 12 counters one at a time onto two heart cards. Ask: how many counters are on one heart card (6). Say: both hearts are 6, because the same shape is always the same number. Then check: put the piles together and count (12). Answer: 6. A child who deals unevenly is asked: are the piles the same?

slides.title: Two lines, same shapes

items: Line 1 tells you the circle.
The circle is the same number in line 2.

slides.note: Round 3, about 4 minutes. Two lines: circle + circle = 6 and circle + triangle = 9. Children use the first line to find the circle (3), then the same circle in the second line to find the triangle (6). They may use counters: 6 on two circle cards, then 9 on one circle card and one triangle card. Ask: what number is the circle (3), the triangle (6). Say: the circle is 3 in both lines. The two lines on the slide are shown first; the two sentences about the circle appear after the children have tried (the next slide). Answers: circle 3, triangle 6. A child who gets a different circle in line 2 is asked: is it the same shape? The numbers are not the sneak-peek numbers: do not tell the sneak-peek answers here.

slides.title: Three rules

items: Each shape is a number.
The same shape is the same number every time.
In our puzzles, different shapes are different numbers.

slides.note: Say the three rules once, slowly. Rule 3 is a rule of our puzzles only (in other maths two shapes can be the same number), so that each puzzle has one answer. Ask: can a circle be 6 in one line and 4 in another line of the same puzzle (no, rule 2). Children answer with a thumb. Never use letters; the shapes are the unknown numbers.

slides.title: Find it, then check it

blocks.head: STEPS
items: Take the square away from the total.
Share what is left between the 2 equal circles.
Check: put the number back into the line.

slides.note: Circle + circle + square = 16 and the square is 4. Take the square away: 16 - 4 = 12 for the two circles. The two circles are equal, so each is 6. Check by putting 6 back into the line: 6 + 6 + 4 = 16. The steps card appears after the questions (next slide); children say each number first. Ask: what is left for the two circles (12); what is one circle (6). Always end with the check.

slides.title: Take one line from another

blocks.head: STEPS
items: Line 1 has one more star than line 2.
The totals show how much that extra star is.
Then put the star into line 2 to find the triangle.

slides.note: Two lines about the same shapes: star + star + triangle = 17 and star + triangle = 12. Line 1 has one more star than line 2, and 17 is 5 more than 12, so one star is 5. Then star + triangle = 12, so 5 + triangle = 12 and the triangle is 7. Ask: how much more is 17 than 12 (5); what is the triangle (7). The steps appear on the next slide, after the children have answered. This is the new idea of the lesson and goes beyond Primary 1: say it was found by taking one line from the other.

slides.title: Check in both lines

blocks.text: Check in every line, not just one.

slides.note: A number that works in one line may not work in another, so we check every line. Line 1: 5 + 5 + 7 = 17. Line 2: 5 + 7 = 12. Both match. Ask: what would we think if line 1 did not match (the numbers are wrong, try again). Link to the Think harder question where a friend gives numbers that work in only one line.

slides.title: A times line

blocks.head: STEPS
items: heart × circle means heart groups of the circle.
How many groups of the circle make the total?
Check: put the number back into the line.

slides.note: A times line: heart × circle = 12 and the circle is 3. Read it as heart groups of 3 make 12. Ask: how many groups of 3 make 12 (4). Children may count in 3s on fingers or put counters in groups of 3. Check: 4 × 3 = 12. Either reading order is accepted in a child answer. Times lines come back in Think harder and Go further.

slides.title: Your turn

blocks.text: Find the star and the heart. Then check both lines.

slides.note: Each child works on their own paper with counters if they like. Star + heart = 11 and star + star + heart = 16. Line 2 has one more star than line 1, and 16 is 5 more than 11, so the star is 5 and the heart is 6. Walk the cameras; do not ask children to hold papers up. Wait 10 seconds before helping. Answers: star 5, heart 6.

slides.title: Check: your turn
slides.note: Answers: star 5, heart 6. Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Children tick their own work with a tick. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

slides.title: Clap and whisper

blocks.text: Count to 20 with me. Clap on 5, 10, 15 and 20.
Whisper the numbers in between.
Stand up. Sip some water.

slides.note: Four minutes. Stand up on camera. Count from 1 to 20 together: children whisper every number and clap loudly on 5, 10, 15 and 20. Then count back from 20 in fives if there is time. No equipment, no running, a little clear space. A child may stay seated. Do not give prizes or compare children.

slides.title: Workbook page 1: Start here

blocks.text: Questions 1 to 4. Take your time.

slides.note: Read questions 1 to 4 aloud. Children work on their own with counters and shape cards; the tutor walks the cameras and asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping. After question 4 any child may choose to carry on or try Think harder. Question 1: a cup hides counters; 11 in all and 3 are loose. Question 2: circle + square = 10 and the square is 4. Question 3: heart + heart = 16. Question 4: three stars make 15.

slides.title: Check page 1
slides.note: Read each answer aloud. Children tick their own page with a tick. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group. Answers: Q1 8; Q2 6; Q3 8; Q4 5.

slides.title: Workbook page 2: Start here

blocks.text: Questions 5 to 7. Take your time.

slides.note: Read questions 5 to 7 aloud. Question 5: two triangles and a square make 14, and the square is 4. Question 6: Ben says the circle is 7; circle + circle = 12. Question 7: 2 bags and 3 loose sweets make 13.

slides.title: Check page 2
slides.note: Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can tick their own work. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group. Answers: Q5 10 and 5; Q6 No, the circle is 6; Q7 10 and 5.

slides.title: Choose your next page

rows: Two lines and a times line
Finish and check your own work

blocks.text: Everyone may choose. Not finished? Pages 3 to 5 are for home too.

slides.note: Invite the whole group at once, for example: when you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation. Never announce who is on which page and never name a child. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Model answers are in the tutor guide. About 5 minutes.

slides.title: Talk and explain

blocks.head: AISHA SAYS
items: Circle + circle = 12.
So circle + circle + circle = 18.

blocks.text: Is Aisha right? How could we check?
I think ... because ...

slides.note: One minute of talk to the grown-up next to you, or to your screen. Children test Aisha with counters: 12 counters on two circle cards is 6 each, and three circle cards of 6 make 18. Then volunteers first; a pass is always fine; never call a child by name to answer. Model answer: yes. The same shape is the same number, so each circle is 6, and three sixes are 18. Repeat each child answer in your own words for the recording.

slides.title: Back to the sneak-peek

blocks.text: The star is 7. The heart is 3. The cup holds 5.

slides.note: Reveal both puzzles now. Say: many of you wrote a good reason. Do not read out anyone earlier answer. Two stars make 14, so one star is 7; the heart and 7 make 10, so the heart is 3. Puzzle 1: 9 counters in all and 4 loose, so the cup holds 5. It was the same idea: a hidden number.

slides.title: Exit ticket

blocks.text: On your own. No looking back.

slides.note: Children answer on page 5. Read E1, E2 and E3 aloud with their totals, and the four options of E2 (the figures on the slide are small). Children tick their own ticket against the next slide. Nobody holds paper to the camera and there is no private chat.

slides.title: Check the exit ticket
slides.note: Read each answer aloud. Children tick their own ticket with a tick. Answers: triangle 9; option 4, the heart is 8; each circle is 7.

slides.title: Look-back
slides.note: Three minutes. Children tick or write the look-back box on page 5. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out. If a child ticks I am still stuck, a grown-up may photograph that page after class and send it to the business WhatsApp (the number is in the parent summary, never on a slide). You then help in the open session next lesson. Never a direct message to a child. The Next time I will try row is optional.

mascot.say: Take your time. You can pass.

slides.title: Well done, inquirers!

blocks.text: Show a grown-up one thing you found out today.

blocks.head: NEXT LESSON
items: Find One First, and the end-of-term check
Have ready: the Term 2 Lesson 10 workbook with its tokens page cut out, 3 to 6 small things, the check sheet in its envelope (keep it closed), a pencil and paper.

slides.note: Say goodbye and thank the grown-ups. Minutes 85 to 90 are flex time: the buffer. If you ran late, finish any open item (the look-back). Do not start anything new. Remind families that next lesson holds the end-of-term check: the sheet and the grown-up note were sent a week before. If the whole class is ahead, show the optional slides and use the Spare-time menu from the tutor guide.

slides.title: Go further: one line or two?

blocks.text: Could the circle be 2? Could it be 3?
What does the second line tell us?

slides.note: Optional, only if you are on time. Line 1 alone has many answers: circle 2 and square 6, circle 3 and square 5, circle 1 and square 7 and more. Line 2 (circle + circle + square = 11) has only one pair that fits both: circle 3 and square 5. Check: 3 + 5 = 8 and 3 + 3 + 5 = 11. Take two answers and move on. This links to the Investigation.

slides.title: If we have time: pick one

rows: Ali says the heart is 5 in one line and 6 in another.
Pick two numbers. Write two lines for your grown-up.
Show a toy how a cup hides a number

blocks.text: Optional. Everyone may join.

slides.note: Optional Spare-time menu, used only if the whole class is ahead. Pick one or two activities (3 to 5 minutes each); full tutor lines and answers are in the tutor guide. Never start new content and never name who is ahead. Slow down with how do you know rather than rushing on. These minutes come from the flex buffer and are not part of the 90-minute sum.

lines.text: @rec
Greet each child by first name as they arrive. Then start the recording. While it runs, avoid names. Check that you can see each child.

Hello, inquirers! Please stay muted unless I invite you to speak. Cameras on if you can, so I can see you; cameras off is fine too. Pencil ready, and your shape cards, counters and two cups on the table.
This lesson is recorded so a friend who is away can catch up. The recording has me, the shared screen and any voice that is unmuted. You may mute and keep your camera off.
Today a shape is a hidden number. The same shape is always the same number. We find it, then we check it.

Say the recording notice in the SAY line above in your own words after the recording has started: the recording has the tutor, the shared screen and any unmuted voice; children may mute and keep the camera off. The routine and the four inquirer rules were introduced earlier in the term: do not re-teach them.

Plain statement for families when it comes up: a box with a hidden number in one line is Primary 1 work, but using the same shape in two lines and taking one line from another go beyond Primary 1 on purpose, always with counters and shape cards.

New here? Say in one minute: our three rule words (notice it, test it, explain why); a guess is fine and you can always pass; after Start here you may choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation; nobody holds paper to the camera. The first recording of the term shows the full routine.
@rec
A box can hide a number. Look at the ten-frame: six counters, and the frame holds ten.
How many more counters fill the frame? Six plus box equals ten.
Box plus three equals eight. What is in the box?
Nine equals five plus box. What is in the box?
Two plates with the same number of counters. Twelve counters in all.
What is five plus five?
Box plus box equals eight, the same number twice. What is in the box?
Seven plus seven?
Four bags with five counters in each bag. Four times five means four groups of five.
How many counters are in four bags of five?
Three groups of four?
Two groups of ten?

If a child is unsure about the box, touch the empty places in the ten-frame and count them. For the same number twice, deal counters one at a time onto two plates. For the bags, add one bag at a time and say the total each time.

Answers: 4, 5, 4; 10, 4, 14; 20, 12, 20. Children answer with a whisper, fingers or hands. Nobody writes. Do not say picture equation yet. Joining cold: all you need is counting to 20 and adding small numbers.
@rec
Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start, and I do not know is welcome. Nobody is marked.
Puzzle one. A cup hides some counters. The cup and 4 loose counters make 9 counters in all. How many counters are in the cup? You may use counters.
Children count out 9 counters or draw, and write the number on their own paper.
Puzzle two. Each shape is a number. Two stars make 14. The heart and a star make 10. How many is the heart? Write it.
Children write or draw their answer.
Keep your paper. Nobody shows it. We will check our own thinking later, at Talk time.
Puzzle 1 answer: 5. Puzzle 2 answer: the star is 7, so the heart is 3. Look for good ideas to praise later (a child who found the star first). Do not write scores or keep a list.
@rec
Your hands are the teachers. Find your circle card and your square card. Count out ten counters. The picture says: circle plus square equals ten. The square is four.
Children count out 10 counters, put 4 on the square card and the rest on the circle card.
How many counters are on the circle card?
The circle is six. We check: six plus four is ten. It matches.
Round two. Heart plus heart equals twelve. Two hearts, so the same number on each.
Children count out 12 counters and deal them one at a time onto two heart cards until the piles match.
How many counters are on one heart card?
Both hearts are six. The same shape is always the same number.
Check it. Put the two piles together. How many counters?
Round three. Two lines. Circle plus circle equals six. Circle plus triangle equals nine. Use line one to find the circle.
Children find the circle from line one, then use the same circle in line two to find the triangle. Counters are fine.
What number is the circle?
What number is the triangle?
The circle was three in both lines. That is our idea for today.

A child who puts a different number for the circle in line 2: ask, is it the same shape? A child who adds all the numbers in a line: ask, what is the total of the line? A child with no shape cards uses a cup or a piece of paper marked with the shape.

Main room only; children say their answers aloud and show fingers; you cannot see counters on small tiles. Answers: circle 6; heart 6 and 12 together; circle 3, triangle 6. Accept any child who finds the numbers by counters or by adding. Do not say equation for every line, say line.
@rec
Three rules for picture equations. One: each shape is a number. Two: the same shape is the same number every time. Three: in our puzzles, different shapes are different numbers.
Can a circle be six in one line and four in another line of the same puzzle? Thumb up or down.
Find it, then check it. Circle plus circle plus square equals sixteen. The square is four.
Take the square away from sixteen. What is left for the two circles?
Two equal circles make twelve. What is one circle?
Now we check. Six plus six plus four equals sixteen. It matches.
Two lines at once. Star plus star plus triangle equals seventeen. Star plus triangle equals twelve. Line one has one more star than line two.
How much more is seventeen than twelve?
So that one extra star is five.
Five plus the triangle makes twelve. What is the triangle?
We always check in both lines. Five plus five plus seven is seventeen. Five plus seven is twelve. Both lines match.
A times line. Heart times circle equals twelve. The circle is three. That means heart groups of three make twelve.
How many groups of three make twelve?
The heart is four. Check: four times three is twelve.
Your turn. Star plus heart equals eleven. Star plus star plus heart equals sixteen. Find the star and the heart. Then check both lines.
Children work on their own paper, with counters if they like. Wait 10 seconds before helping.
The star is five. The heart is six. Tick your own work with a tick.

Key words to use every time: shape, line, the same number, check. Say take one line from the other. Never use letters. Beyond Primary 1 on purpose: using the same shape in two lines, taking one line from another and the times line. Do not teach a rule to recite; the counters are the method.

If a child adds every number they see, ask: which numbers does the line really give us? If a child cannot start with two lines, make the second line smaller with counters: 11 counters, then 16 counters, and ask what is extra.
@rec
Stand up and get a sip of water. I count from one. Whisper every number, and clap loudly on five, ten, fifteen and twenty.
Count 1 to 20 together: whisper the numbers and clap on 5, 10, 15 and 20. Then count back from 20 in fives. Children may stay seated.
@rec

Page 1, Start here. Question 1: a cup hides some counters. 3 counters are outside the cup. There are 11 counters in all. How many counters are in the cup? Question 2: each shape is a number. Circle plus square equals 10. The square is 4. Find the number for the circle. Question 3: heart plus heart equals 16. Find the number for the heart. Question 4: star plus star plus star equals 15. Find the number for the star.
Page 1, questions 1 to 4. Tutor walks the cameras, asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping.

start.text: A cup hides some counters. 3 counters are outside the cup. There are 11 counters in all. Fill in the blank.
start.hint: Take the 3 loose counters away from 11.
start.solution: 11 - 3 = 8, so the cup holds 8 counters. Check: 8 + 3 = 11.

start.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for the circle.
start.hint: Take the square away from the total: 10 - 4.
start.solution: The total is 10 and the square is 4. 10 - 4 = 6, so the circle is 6. Check: 6 + 4 = 10.

start.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for the heart.
start.hint: Two hearts are the same number. Share 16 between the two hearts.

start.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for the star.
start.hint: The 3 stars are the same number. Share 15 between 3 stars.

start.text: Each shape is a number. The square is 4. Fill in the blanks.
start.hint: Take the square away from 14 first.
start.solution: 14 - 4 = 10, so the 2 triangles make 10. The triangles are the same, so each is 5. Check: 5 + 5 + 4 = 14.

start.text: Ben says the circle is 7. Look at the picture.

parts.text: Is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No.

start.hint: Put 7 into both circles. What is the total?
start.solution: 7 + 7 = 14, but the line says 12. So Ben is not correct. 6 + 6 = 12, so the circle is 6.
mistakes: Saying Yes because 7 is close to 6.

start.text: Each bag has the same number of sweets. 3 sweets are outside the bags. There are 13 sweets in all. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: The 2 bags have [2] sweets in all.

start.hint: Take the 3 loose sweets away from 13.
start.solution: 13 - 3 = 10 sweets are in the 2 bags. 5 + 5 = 10, so each bag has 5 sweets. Check: 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.
mistakes: Writing 6 (13 shared between 2 bags, ignoring the loose sweets).

think.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for each shape. Show your working.
think.hint: Line 1 has one more square than line 2. How much more is 19 than 13?
think.solution: Line 1 has one more square than line 2, and 19 is 6 more than 13, so the square is 6. Then 6 + heart = 13, so the heart is 7. Check: 6 + 6 + 7 = 19.
mistakes: Finding the square but forgetting the heart.

think.text: Kumar says the heart is 8 and the star is 7. Look at the picture. Decide if each statement is True or False.
think.hint: Put 8 and 7 into each line and add.
think.solution: Line 1: 8 + 7 = 15, which matches. Line 2: 8 + 8 + 7 = 23, but the line says 21. Kumar's numbers work in line 1 only.
mistakes: Saying line 2 is true because 23 is close to 21.

tf.s: Line 1 is true with Kumar's numbers.
Line 2 is true with Kumar's numbers.

think.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for each shape.
think.hint: Line 1 gives the heart. Then use the heart in line 2.
think.solution: The 2 hearts make 6, so the heart is 3. Then 3 × circle = 15 means 3 groups of 5 make 15, so the circle is 5. Check: 3 × 5 = 15.

go.text: Each shape is a number. Find the number for each shape.
go.hint: Start with the line that has only one kind of shape.
go.solution: Circle × circle = 25, so the circle is 5 (5 groups of 5). Then heart + 5 = 12, so the heart is 7. Then star - 7 = 4, so the star is 11. Check: 11 - 7 = 4.
mistakes: Taking 4 away from 7 and writing 3 for the star.

go.text: Each shape is a number. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: One star and one heart make [2].

go.hint: Put the two lines together. How many stars and hearts are there?
go.solution: Both lines together have 3 stars and 3 hearts, and 22 + 20 = 42. 3 stars and 3 hearts make 42, so one star and one heart make 14. Then 22 - 14 = 8 is a star, and 14 - 8 = 6 is a heart.

go.text: Each shape is a number. The heart is greater than the triangle. Find the number for each shape.
go.hint: Which two numbers add to 9? Try pairs and multiply each pair.
go.solution: The pairs that add to 9 are 1 and 8, 2 and 7, 3 and 6, 4 and 5. Only 4 and 5 multiply to 20. The heart is greater, so the heart is 5 and the triangle is 4.
mistakes: Using 3 and 6 (they add to 9 but multiply to 18).

investigation.title: One line or two?
investigation.first: The circle + the triangle = 10. One pair: circle 2, triangle 8. Write 2 more.
investigation.text: The circle + the circle + the triangle = 14. Do any pairs fit both lines? Why?
investigation.answer: Only circle 4 and triangle 6 fit both lines. One line alone has many pairs that fit (1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5 and more; accept 5 and 5 for line 1). 5 and 5 fails line 2 (5 + 5 + 5 = 15, not 14). The second line is the same as the first with one more circle, and 14 is 4 more than 10, so the circle is 4.
investigation.look_for: A child who tries pairs for both lines, finds that only one pair works, or says one line is not enough to find two numbers. Credit any clear reason. Do not mark a child down for stopping at one pair.
mistakes: Choosing a pair that fits line 1 only, such as 5 and 5 (it makes 15 in line 2).

exit.text: Each shape is a number. The triangle + the triangle = 18. Find the number for the triangle.
The heart + the square = 13. The square is 5. Find the number for the heart. Choose the correct answer. Write its number in the bracket.
mistakes: Choosing (1) 5, the number of the square.
Choosing (2) 6 or (3) 7 after a counting slip.

exit.text: Each shape is a number. The star is 5. Find the number for each circle.
exit.solution: 19 - 5 = 14, so the 2 circles make 14. 7 + 7 = 14, so each circle is 7. Check: 7 + 7 + 5 = 19.

talk.question: Aisha says: circle + circle = 12, so circle + circle + circle = 18. Is Aisha right? How could we check?
talk.answer: Yes. The same shape is the same number, so each circle is 6 (12 shared between two). Three circles are 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. We can check with counters: 12 on two cards is 6 on each, then add a third card of 6.
talk.look_for: A child who finds the circle first, or who uses counters or a picture. Not just yes or no.

home_practice.text: Each shape is a number. The star + the star = 8. Find the number for the star. ___
A cup hides some counters. The cup and 5 loose counters make 14 counters in all. How many counters are in the cup? ___
The heart is 4. What is the heart + the heart + the heart? ___
Line 1: the circle + the circle + the triangle = 15. Line 2: the circle + the triangle = 9. Find the number for the triangle. ___
home_practice.solution: Line 1 has one more circle than line 2, and 15 - 9 = 6, so the circle is 6. Then 6 + triangle = 9, so the triangle is 3.

home_practice.text: Line 1: the circle × the circle = 16. Line 2: the heart + the circle = 9. (× means groups of.) Find the number for the heart. ___
home_practice.solution: Line 1: 4 × 4 = 16 (4 groups of 4), so the circle is 4. Line 2: heart + 4 = 9, so the heart is 5.

menu.title: Can a shape change?
menu.tutor: Ali says: the heart is 5 in line 1 and 6 in line 2, and both lines are fine. Is that allowed? Test it with counters: put the same heart card into both lines.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Ali says the heart is 5 in one line and 6 in another. Is that allowed? Test it with counters.
menu.answer: No. The same shape is the same number in every line. If the heart is 5 in line 1 it must be 5 in line 2 too. If the numbers do not fit, one of them is wrong, so check again.

menu.title: Make a puzzle for your grown-up
menu.tutor: Pick a number for the circle and a different number for the star. Write two lines, such as circle + star = a total and circle + circle + star = a total. Ask your grown-up to find your numbers.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Pick two numbers. Write two lines for a grown-up to solve, then check their answer.
menu.answer: No single answer. Check the totals: with circle 4 and star 6, line 1 is 10 and line 2 is 14. The grown-up takes one line from the other.

menu.title: Teach it back
menu.tutor: Pretend your grown-up or a toy has never met a picture equation. Use a cup and counters to show how a shape can hide a number.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Show a grown-up how a cup can hide a number and how to find it.
menu.answer: A cup and 4 loose counters make 9 in all. Count out 9, take the 4 away, and the rest is what the cup holds: 5.

parent.summary: We met picture equations: a shape is a hidden number, and the same shape is always the same number. We found hidden numbers with counters, checked them, and took one line from another to find two shapes. One hidden number in a line, like 4 + box = 10, is Primary 1 work; using one shape in two lines, taking one line from another and a times line go past the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. We use shapes, never letters.
words: check: put the number back into the line
take one line from another: find the extra shape
try_home: Hidden cup: put 5 counters in a cup, add 4 loose ones, and say the total is 9. How many are in the cup?
Two cups: put the same number of counters in two cups and say the total is 12. How many in each cup?
Your turn to hide: your child hides counters in a cup and tells you the total. Can you find the number?
ask: How can you check your number in the line?
parent.when_stuck: Let your child use counters and two cups, and wait 10 seconds before helping. Asking ‘what is the total?’ works better than giving the answer. Please do not teach a rule or letters: counters and a cup are enough. If the look-back page says ‘I am still stuck’, photograph it and send it to our business WhatsApp (+65 9880 5962). Photos are kept 90 days after the program ends.
parent.next: Term 2 Lesson 10: Find One First, with the end-of-term check. It has one picture-equation question: if your child missed this lesson, do workbook pages 1 and 2 first. Online practice: your tutor will share the link.

safeguarding: Counters, cups and small things stay on the table: nothing goes in the mouth or ears. No matches, toothpicks or anything sharp. Keep small things away from younger brothers and sisters. Cups stay on the table so that nothing is spilled.
This lesson uses the main room only: no breakout rooms, so the tutor sees every camera. A parent sits nearby but does not give answers.

Nobody holds paper or a board up to the camera: a gallery view shows everyone. Children tick their own work against the answer slide, answer together on a count of three, or show fingers or a thumb for a choice. There is no private chat.

Never read out a child’s name with a right or wrong answer. The recording has the tutor, the shared screen and any voice that is unmuted. Children may mute and keep their cameras off. A child’s page is never shown.
Movement break: children need a little clear space, soft shoes or socks on a safe floor, no stairs and no running. Counting aloud is quiet; a child may stay seated.

A child who is still stuck ticks ‘I am still stuck’ on the look-back page. A grown-up may photograph that page after class and send it to the business WhatsApp only; photos are kept for 90 days after the program ends. The tutor then helps in the open session next lesson. No private messages to children, and no personal phones.
The look-back is never collected in front of the group or read out. A pass is always allowed.
tutor_prep: Solve every workbook question yourself first. Check that each shape in a puzzle is a different number (T1: 6 and 7; T2: 6 and 9; T3: 3 and 5; G1: 5, 7 and 11; G2: 8 and 6; G3: 5 and 4) so you can answer a child who asks.

Tell parents a week before: print the workbook pages and the kit page (a grown-up cuts out the 20 counters), draw four shape cards (a circle, a square, a triangle and a heart on four small pieces of paper), and find about 30 counters or buttons and two cups. Small things stay away from mouths and younger children. Next lesson holds the end-of-term check: with this lesson's materials, send the check sheet (in a closed envelope) and the grown-up note.
Have the slides open. Have your own shape cards, a cup and counters to show on camera if you wish.

Check the recording captures the tutor and the shared screen. Children video is excluded; any unmuted voice is recorded. Greet each child by first name as they arrive, then start the recording, then say the notice; avoid first names while it runs.

Be plain with families: one line with a hidden number is Primary 1 work, but using the same shape in two lines, taking one line from another and the times line are beyond the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. Do not call the lesson MOE-aligned. Never use letters for unknowns; shapes and boxes only. The counters are the method, not a rule to recite.

Slides s-explore3, s-m2 and s-m3 keep the method off the screen while you ask: the steps appear on the slide after. Read every question with its totals and the four options of E2 aloud: the figures on the slides are small.
